rationale: Greek γέεννα; the eschatological place of punishment. Standard transliteration with Lyc. ⲣⲉⲉⲛⲛⲁ for γέεννα. Used in opposition to ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ / ⲡⲭⲓⲥⲉ as the lower-cosmic destination from which the seal of faith protects the catechumen.

Lyc. reflex of ϩⲧⲟ 'horse' with ⲍ for ϩ (regular Lyc. orthographic feature). Central image of the parable on this page: the king's sealed horse that cannot be stolen, paralleling the sealed catechumen who cannot be brought to Gehenna.

Lyc. variant of ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, signet' (already attested in glossary as ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ on the King-of-Darkness body-part schema). Here in moral-soteriological register: the seal of faith and knowledge stamped upon the catechumen's soul corresponds typologically to the king's seal upon his horse.

Already in glossary; here used distributively in line 6: ⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ ⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ 'peoples and peoples' = various ethnic/communal contexts in which the apostle finds prospective catechumens. Plural-distributive doubling expresses the universality of his missionary work.

Greek αἵρεσις with Lyc. ⲍ-onset (regular for Greek words with rough breathing). Used distributively: 'heresies, heresies' = various sectarian contexts from which the apostle chooses by his speech of light. Standard Manichaean polemical term for rival religious-philosophical schools.

Greek μανία 'madness, frenzy.' Used here as the negative counterpart to ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ 'Error' — the works of the peoples that exist 'in madness' as the affective register of cosmic confusion before conversion.
Lyc. compound preposition ϩⲓϫⲱⲱϥ 'upon him' with regular ⲍ for ϩ and ⲭ for ϫ. Standard locative-resultative preposition for the seal placed upon the horse / the seal placed upon the soul.

Apparent Lyc. compound verbal form combining ⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ root with subject and object affixes. The form (heavenly μορφή) maintains its protective trust-relation with the catechumen below. Etymology and exact morphology uncertain; flagged for parallels.
